methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $23M total raised proxy.

private.name: Cover
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series B)

data.narrative:
Cuby Technologies is a Series B-stage housing and construction company founded by Aleks Gampel and Aleh Kandrashou. The company has raised $23.4M to date. The relevant comparable universe is limited, comprising one identified private peer (Cover) and no direct public comparables in the sector.

Valuation analysis applies a stage-progression methodology, leveraging the $23.4M total raised as a valuation proxy. Using a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $44M. This represents a reasonable progression from deployed capital, consistent with risk-adjusted return expectations at this stage. The single-method constraint reflects limited public market data and a narrow private comparable set, which reduces triangulation depth.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $38M (low) to $51M (high), with a median point of $44M. Key uncertainties include the absence of a robust public comp universe for benchmarking, reliance on a single private peer, and limited visibility into Cuby's unit economics relative to Cover. The stage-progression method is applicable but would benefit from supplementary revenue multiple or DCF analysis if additional operational metrics become available.
